tossups.text: One of these things was called an ónoma in Ancient Greece, and X-bar theory replaced one which said "S" is equivalent to "VP" plus one of these things. Determiners are combined with these things, which usually serve as specifiers in inflectional phrases. In many European languages, the word for these things is a cognate of "substantive." Some languages distinguish the alienable and inalienable types of these things. Nominalization results in certain words becoming these things. In a typical English sentence structure, the predicate directs a type of this part of speech called the subject. For 10 points, name these parts of speech, usually described as people, places, or things.

Moseley's law states that this quantity is proportional to the square root of frequency in an element. Elements with the same value for this property but different numbers of neutrons are called isotopes. The atomic mass of an element is the sum of this value and the number of neutrons. For 10 points, name this property of an element that is the number of protons in an atom of that element.

Many images of the Venus de Milo appear in one painting by this artist dedicated to his wife Gala. An array of brick-like objects appears in a painting by this artist named for the "Disintegration" of one of his previous paintings. In a painting by this artist inspired by Camembert cheese, melting clocks appear in a Catalonian landscape. For 10 points, what Spanish surrealist painted The Persistence of Memory?

While working in this industry in Russia, James McNeill Whistler's father George Washington Whistler introduced a design by William Howe that involves vertical members in compression. Two serfs of the Demidov family, the Cherepanov brothers, were freed for an invention in this industry. Franz Gerstner rejected the inclined plane approach used in this industry, which benefited from the Li-Lobanov Treaty in northeastern China. Legendarily, Tsar Nicholas I's finger caused misdrafted plans in this industry, leading to a structure with a conspicuous bend. Sergei Witte ("VIT-uh") championed a project in this industry which the Czechoslovak Legion seized during the Russian Civil War. For 10 points, name this industry that operates a "Trans-Siberian" service from Moscow to Vladivostok.

A list of prominent people in this state, the Four Hundred, was created by socialite Ward McAllister. Violence during the Orange Riots led to the downfall of a leader in this state. In an 1871 illustration, a politician from this state was caricatured with a money bag replacing his head. Chester A. Arthur was fired from this state's U.S. Customs House in 1878 by Rutherford B. Hayes, who became president after defeating this state's governor Samuel Tilden. William "Boss" Tweed once led a corrupt political machine in this state. For 10 points, Tammany Hall once dominated what state's politics from Manhattan?

They're not swords, but Roman records state that a long-standing trade in these weapons was carried on with the land of Agisymba by the Garamantes. Ironically, a general named Nicanor, who was nicknamed for these weapons, was on the losing side of a battle in which they were used to crush phalangites near Cynoscephalae. The Romans named a variety of these weapons after the region of Lucania after the Battle of Heraclea, in which Pyrrhus of Epirus used them. Tactics invented to defeat these weapons included releasing flaming pigs and opening ranks and then surrounding them, as done at the Battle of Zama. Chandragupta Maurya secured a treaty with the Seleucids by gifting 500 of these animals. For 10 points, name these large beasts famously brought over the Alps by Hannibal.

This character "turned cold with horror" after seeing a pony be swallowed by the Grimpen Mire in a novel in which they are told to "Go back to London" after being mistaken for Sir Henry by Beryl Stapleton. This character explains a scar on his shoulder from a jezail bullet in a book he narrates about Jefferson Hope. This character proposes to Mary Morstan at the end of The Sign of the Four, and he becomes a biographer after seeing all the credit go to Gregson and Lestrade in A Study in Scarlet. For 10 points, name this veteran war doctor who lives at 221B Baker Street with Sherlock Holmes.
acceptableAnswers: Late of the Army Medical Department

tossups.text: While attempting a publicity stunt for a movement promoting this right, Emily Davison was fatally trampled by a horse. Two early organizations in favor of this right merged to form NAWSA, which was led at one point by Carrie Chapman Catt. Wyoming was the first state to grant this right. The Declaration of Sentiments , penned by Elizabeth Cady Stanton, demanded this right at the Seneca Falls convention. For 10 points, name this right championed by Susan B. Anthony, which was granted by the 19th Amendment.

One of this author's title characters is dissuaded from leading a violent rebellion after he hears Milly singing a gospel; in that book, Edward Clayton tries to win a court case to impress Nina Gordon. This author wrote a novel in which James Marvyn is lost at sea, causing Mary Scudder to accept the reverend Samuel Hopkins's proposal. One of this author's characters, Tom Loker, becomes a Quaker after being shot by George Harris. This author of "A Tale of the Great Dismal Swamp," Dred, and The Minister's Wooing created a character who bonds with Eva St. Claire before being beaten and then killed by Simon Legree. She also created Eliza, who crosses the frozen Ohio River with her young child during her bid for freedom. For 10 points, name this author who inspired the anti-slavery movement with her book Uncle Tom's Cabin.

On the eve of revolution, this man's political career began when he failed to lead a peasant militia to defend king Frederick William IV. Agreements negotiated by this man include the peace of Nikolsburg and the Convention of Gastein, which guaranteed the annexation of Schleswig-Holstein. He negotiated the Triple Alliance with Russia and Austro-Hungary and fought against the influence of the Catholic Church's in the "Kulturkampf," but was later sacked by Kaiser Wilhelm II. For 10 points, name this unifier of Germany who had a famous WWII-Era battleship named after him.

While leafing through a book of paintings, a woman in this film comments that another character is a "Botticelli angel." For this film, the cinematographer Russell Boyd imitated impressionist paintings by draping bridal veils over the camera. This film opens with a girl quoting Poe's line "What we see and what we seem are but a dream - a dream within a dream." Late in this film, a gardener finds the body of the orphan Sara, who had earlier been forced to stay at Appleyard College while the other students left. This film based on a Joan Lindsay novel mostly takes place on Valentine's Day in 1900, when Miranda, Marion, Irma, and Edith mysteriously collapse near a monolith. For 10 points, name this Peter Weir film in which a group of Australian schoolgirls disappear during the title outing.

During this initiative, the National Endowment for Arts and Humanities was established. John Gardner, the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare, helped pass the Secondary Education Act and created the Corporation for Public Broadcasting as part of this program. Medicare and the Head Start programs were created during this initiative, and Congress passed two Civil Rights acts and one Voting Rights act. For 10 points, identify this initiative that also included a War on Poverty, a set of liberal social reforms created by Lyndon B. Johnson.

Deceased members of this religion may have their frontal bones removed from their skulls, packed in ice, and stored in a Swiss bank vault in preparation for their eventual resurrection. This religion promotes the practice of "sensual meditation" and holds four annual "seminars" that feature an initiation ritual called "transmission of the cellular plan." This religion advocates the creation of a world government with 144 divisions based on the doctrines of "economic humanitarianism" and "geniocracy." In 2002, a member of this religion's all-female Order of Angels named Brigitte Boisselier claimed to have facilitated the birth of the first human clone. While hiking in the volcanic crater of Puy de Lassolas, this religion's founder supposedly met a four-foot tall humanoid who asked him to build an embassy and prepare for the return of the Elohim to Earth. For 10 points, name this UFO cult founded by French race car driver Claude Vorilhon.

Patterns of similar fossils appearing far apart were used as evidence for this phenomenon, which was supported by the discovery of magnetic "stripes" around the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The fact that South America and Africa fit neatly into each other led Alfred Wegener to propose this phenomenon. For 10 points, what phenomenon is now known to result from the movement of tectonic plates causing large landmasses to slowly move across the Earth?
acceptableAnswers: descriptive answers like the movement of tectonic plates

tossups.text: In this novel, a carriage accident takes the life of the blind Pew, and the narrator is injured by Israel Hands. The protagonist borrows a coracle from Ben Gunn. In this work, Dr. Livesay and Squire Trelawney embark on a voyage headed by Captain Smollett after the death of Billy Bones. One character escapes the Black Spot after revealing a certain map. For 10 points, what work by Robert Louis Stevenson is narrated by Jim Hawkins and tells of the pirate Long John Silver?

Among his consorts are Grid, Rind, and Jord. Son of Bor and Bestla, this god has a ring, Draupnir, which duplicates itself nine times over every night, and he rides the eight-legged steed Sleipnir. He gave one of his eyes to the giant Mimir in order to drink from the giant's well of knowledge. For 10 points, name this Norse god, father of Thor.

Some cells within this structure are anchored from below by Deiters' cells and pillar cells. The protein prestin is found in certain cells in this structure whose stereocilia projections bend in response to pressure. When this structure's oval window is stimulated by the stapes (STAY-peez), the endolymph in this structure moves through channels lined with hair cells. Surgeons commonly restore hearing by placing "implants" in, for 10 points, what snail-shaped organ that converts sound into nerve signals in the inner ear?

The poet wrote that this poem's third and fourth quatrains could be played for comedy, specifically in the images of the title character, who "with rod" made the lazy geese scuttle "from their noon apple-dreams." The second stanza says of the title character, "Her wars were bruited in our high window," while the poem opens by remarking "There was such speed in her little body, / And such lightness in her footfall." Robert Penn Warren claimed that the poem's effect was embodied in the words astonishes and vexed in a study of the poet, Penn Warren's former teacher. FTP, name this elegy written on the death of a neighbor's youngest girl, a poem by John Crowe Ransom.
acceptableAnswers: The Bells for John Whiteside’s Daughter

tossups.text: In human anatomy, this structure is essential for appendicular skeleton. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this skull-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The skull is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in appendicular skeleton.

tossups.text: [description acceptable] The Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba are a pair of illustrated scrolls illustrating these events and were commissioned by one participant, Takezaki Suenaga. One of these actions was initiated by a letter written by king Chungyeol. The first of these events is also known as the Battle of Bun'ei, while the second, seven years later, is referred to as the Kōan Campaign. Both culminated at Hakata Bay, which is now part of the city of Fukuoka. For 10 points, name these failed attacks, ordered in 1274 and 1281 by Kublai Khan and turned back in part due to two conveniently-timed typhoons that became known as 'divine winds', or kamikaze?
acceptableAnswers: Battles of Hakata Bay before mentioned

parts.text: Name this type of message that titles a 1928 book by Edward Bernays. Noam Chomsky and Edward S. Herman advance a model of mass media named for this type of message in Manufacturing Consent.
The title of Manufacturing Consent comes from this media theorist, who called the public the "bewildered herd." He also introduced the modern meaning of "stereotype."
Manufacturing Consent, which discusses anticommunist bias in the media, was written during this period of tension between the US and USSR. This period's two-word name was popularized by Lippmann.

bonuses.leadin: This term first described a college that trained Catholic missionaries. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these organs which contain Bowman's capsule and the Loop of Henle.
This functional unit of the kidney contains the glomerulus and a renal tubule.
The kidneys' primary function in the body is to filter blood and produce this bodily fluid, which is then stored in the bladder.

bonuses.leadin: The most common cancer of this organ in children is a Wilms tumor. For 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this song that ends with Romeo asking, "Marry me Juliet, you'll never have to be alone?" The music video features the singer waiting for her beloved in the countryside.
This country singer's "Love Story" appears on her album Fearless. She has also scored hits with "Our Song" and "Teardrops on My Guitar."
This musician, who wrote "Live Like You Were Dying" and "Something Like That" and is married to Faith Hill, and is the title focus of a Swift song from her first album.

bonuses.leadin: This song asks "Romeo, save me" because the singer has been "feelin' so alone." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this name also held by a pharaoh dubbed "the Great" whose forces won the Battle of Kadesh.
The Harem Conspiracy centered around Ramesses III's visit to this city for a Heb-Sed festival. The Karnak temple complex was located in this city, whose ruins are found in modern-day Luxor.

The trials from the Harem Conspiracy were recorded on a papyrus now located in this city. Another papyrus located in a museum in this city is the most extensive list of pharaohs and dates to the reign of Ramesses II.

bonuses.leadin: A pharaoh with this name was targeted by the queen Tiye in the Harem Conspiracy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this "Baron," who was tasked by Napoleon III to carry out a massive renovation program for the capital city; critics found this man's work too extravagant.
Haussmann renovated this city located on the Seine River.
This Italian revolutionary tried to kill Napoleon III in 1858 by throwing bombs at the imperial carriage. He failed and was guillotined later that year.

bonuses.leadin: This man asked for the title "aqueduc," making a pun on the words "duke" and "aqueduct." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this group, whose leader Gaspard de Coligny ("gas-PARR duh koh-leen-YEE") was assassinated in 1572. His assassination sparked the Saint Bartholomew's Day massacre, which targeted this religious minority.

The Edict of Nantes was revoked by a 1685 edict named after this palace. That edict named after this palace ended state tolerance for Protestantism, and allowed persecution of Huguenots by billeting dragoons in their homes.
This king issued the Edict of Fontainebleau as part of his campaign against Protestantism. This so-called "Sun King" ruled France for over 72 years.

bonuses.leadin: This group received significant rights in France under the terms of the 1598 Edict of Nantes ("nont"). For 10 points each:

parts.text: This author's essays include "The English Mail Coach" and "On the Knocking at the Gate in Macbeth." His most famous work tells of his addiction to laudanum.
This author's book The Doors of Perception details his experiences with the drug mescaline. In his novel Brave New World, residents of the World State take the drug soma.
This author of many conversation poems wrote about a "damsel with a dulcimer" and the sacred river Alph in a poem that was inspired by an opium-induced dream.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these writers who used drugs.

parts.text: Name this June 28, 1914 event that was accomplished by Gavrilo Princip. It triggered anti-Serbian demonstrations in Austria-Hungary, the July Crisis, and, eventually, World War I.
The assassination took place in this Austro-Hungarian city, now the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Princip was a member of this pro-Serbian terrorist group, which organized the attack of Franz Ferdinand's motorcade.

bonuses.leadin: After failing to accomplish this event with a bomb, Nedeljko Cabrinovic [neh-dyell-koh kah-bree- noh-vich] failed to commit suicide by swallowing weak cyanide and jumping into a five-inch deep river. For 10 points each,

parts.text: A missionary develops an unhealthy relationship with an idol known as Fetish in "The Renegade," a story that appears in this author's collection, Exile and the Kingdom.

In this collection's story "Hands," Adolph Myers is fired from his teaching position due to an unfortunate tendency to caress his students, leading him to change his name to Wing Biddlebaum. Wing is one of the residents of the title town of this Sherwood Anderson collection.
In this novel by J.G. Ballard, the protagonist becomes a follower of Dr. Robert Vaughan after he begins fetishizing car accidents.

bonuses.leadin: Answer some questions about fetishes in literature. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this country where Mutesa II held power after it gained independence. This country underwent a "Move to the Left" under Milton Obote.

Milton Obote was himself overthrown this by this dictator, who had led a military force to expel Mutesa II. This man, who allowed Palestinian hijackers to land at Entebbe, took many fanciful titles such as "Last King of Scotland" while ruling during the 1970s.
When Idi Amin expelled all Asians from Uganda in 1972, most of them were of this ethnicity of Mohandas Gandhi. They speak a namesake language in India's westernmost state.

bonuses.leadin: A one-time kabaka or king of this modern-day nation was called "King Freddie" by British newspapers and was exiled for two years until he returned as a constitutional monarch. For 10 points each:

parts.text: With his brother Hubert, this artist created the Ghent Altarpiece. He also painted The Arnolfini Wedding.

This artist's version of The Descent from the Cross shows a skull below a fainting Mary and puts Jesus in a T-shape pose. He painted the birth, death, and resurrection of Jesus in the Miraflores Altarpiece.

This artist created a richly colored depiction of the Adoration of the Magi called the Monforte Altarpiece. Some credited Andrea del Castagno with creating this artist's famous depiction of the Adoration of the Shepherds.

bonuses.leadin: Name some Early Netherlandish painters, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Dozens of attempts have been made to create a U.S. Constitutional amendment banning the act of protest bysetting this object on fire. The U.S. Code notes that proper disposal of this object, when torn or faded, shouldinclude setting it on fire.
White supremacists like the KKK adopted the Scottish tradition of the crann-tara, the burning of thissymbol, as an intimidation tactic.
On July 4th, 1854, this abolitionist and publisher ofThe Liberatorpublicly burned a copy of the U.S.Constitution, calling it "a Covenant with Death, an Agreement with Hell."

bonuses.leadin: Give the following about inflammatory protests, for ten points each.

parts.text: Identify this process which often involved removing the organs and placing them in canopic jars in preparation for a meeting with Anubis.

Some textual evidence for mummification comes from the account of this figure in the Old Testament. This man goes to Haran where he works for his uncle Laban for seven years in order to marry Laban's daughter.

Some Egyptian spirits in the afterlife would meet the Ennead, a group of gods including this deity whose lonely masturbation sessions created Shu and Tefnut. Unlike a similar deity, he did not wear a double crown.

bonuses.leadin: A low-cost form of this process involved a thorough rinsing with syrmaea and then a steeping in natrum for seventy days. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this quantity that describes how often an event occurs, measured in Hertz.
This technology which emits waves with higher frequency than humans can hear is often used to create images of fetuses in the womb.
The frequency of a musical note is usually described by this five-letter word.

bonuses.leadin: For waves, this quantity is equal to velocity divided by wavelength. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this famously long set of novels whose protagonist recalls parts of his life over a cup of tea.
acceptableAnswers: A la recherché du temps perdu
The In Search of Lost Time

parts.text: This twentieth-century French author wrote In Search of Lost Time.
In the first volume of In Search of Lost Time, Marcel remembers his life after biting into a tea soaked one of these objects.

bonuses.leadin: Its seven volumes include Cities of the Plain and Swann's Way. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This tetralogy by T.H. White begins with the novel The Sword And The Stone, and it's title references the prophecy that Arthur will become king again sometime in the future. It was found to actually have a 5th book, The Book of Merlyn.

This compilation of tales and translations by the violent criminal Sir Thomas Malory was written while he was imprisoned. It is divided into 21 books, and much of it's narrative structure is credited to the printer Thomas Caxton.

This Welsh compilation of tales was based on The White Book of Rhydderch and The Red Book of Hergest and one part deals with the conflict between Pryderi and math. It's Three Romances focus on Owain, Peredur, Geraint, and Enid, and is cited as a source for Chretien's Arthurian romances.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these works which deal with Arthurian myth For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these branching cells that are divided by selectively permeable septa.
The entirety of a fungus's vegetative mass of hyphae is given this name.
Fungi contain this protein, a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine subunits, in their cell walls. It is also found in the exoskeleton of arthropods.

bonuses.leadin: These filamentous cells have structures at their tips called spitzenkorper that organize their growth. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author who wrote in a "feigned hand" to anonymously publish her first novel, whose title woman enters London society and marries Lord Orville despite the scheming of her grandmother Madame Duval.

Burney's address to Nobody references the Odyssey, which this later British author claimed was actually written by a Sicilian woman. This author wrote a novel set in a utopia whose name is an anagram for the word "nowhere."
Burney was called the "mother of English fiction" by this author, who "ventured to guess that Anon, who wrote so many poems without signing them, was often a woman" in her essay A Room of One's Own.

bonuses.leadin: At age fifteen, this author began her diary with an address to Nobody before questioning, "but why, permit me to ask, must a female be made Nobody?" For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with sebaceous glands.
What is the main function of the hair follicle in the integumentary system?
Name another component of the integumentary system related to sebaceous glands.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human integumentary system.

parts.text: Give this Roman name for the region inhabited by tribes such as the Marcomanni, Suebi, and Alemanni.

A major source for ancient Germanic culture comes from the Germania by this Roman author of the Annals and the Histories. This historian may have spelled the word "Christian" with an e in his account of the crucifixion.

Tacitus' Germania may intentionally emphasize the freedom of the Germans in contrast to the dictatorial rule of this Roman emperor who was the last ruler of the Flavian dynasty. This emperor was succeeded by Nerva.

bonuses.leadin: A military disaster in this region was often called the Clades Variana because of Varus, who led three legions to destruction here. For 10 points each:
